I will do it mostly the way I know works here. I have 9.2 mu, only 2 people in the house, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will keep the cabbage-chinesecabbage-spinach rotation on the better piece because I have done that before and the well water lets me push the crop when it turns dry. For seed, I will use hybrid on cabbage, chili, chinesecabbage, and eggplant because I have seen neighbors get steadier heads and better selling yield that way. For kidney bean and spinach, I will stay closer to the old way and not spend too much. On fertilizer, I will not cut too hard. If I save a little fertilizer and lose the crop, that is worse than wasting some money. So I will put enough base manure and compound fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen after the crop stands up well. Cabbage, chinesecabbage, and eggplant eat more, so I will feed them heavier. Kidney bean fixes some strength by itself, so I will hold nitrogen lower. I will use rotary tillage on most plots because it is quicker on 9.2 mu and I can finish on time. With water from the well, I will irrigate after transplanting or emergence, then again at heading, flowering, or pod filling depending on the crop. I will spray when I usually see trouble, not wait too long, because worms and disease can take profit fast.
